name: Technical Support and Service Desk
summary: Half the job is technical; the other half is understanding the person on the other side and recording what was done.
prerequisites: Requires the three operating systems. Half of this course is not technical — it is the conversation with the person on the other side.
syllabus: A diagnostic method: from symptom to cause
Ethics, privacy and the limits of the role
topics: A diagnostic method: reproduce, isolate, test and confirm
Asking the right question: what the user did, not what they thought
Layers of cause: user, application, system, network and hardware
Service without jargon: explaining without belittling anyone
Recording tickets: what to note and why
Priority, urgency and service level agreements (SLA)
Escalation: when to pass it on and with what information
Runbooks: a written procedure for the recurring problem
A knowledge base and documentation another technician can follow
Remote access: tools, consent and logging
Communicating with other areas: management, HR, legal and vendors
Ethics and privacy: what you see and what you do not repeat
The limits of the role: when the answer is "I cannot do that"
An overview of entry-level certifications: CompTIA A+, Linux+ and Network+
